title: Best Intercom alternatives for 2027
summary: Fin is now owned by Salesforce. Seven alternatives sorted by use case and vertical fit, so you can shortlist without sitting through seven demos.
body_markdown:
## Full helpdesk replacements


If you're leaving Intercom as a platform, not just evaluating the AI, these are two of the strongest landing spots.


### Zendesk


[Zendesk](https://yuma.ai/blogs/zendesk-ai-alternatives) is the most-cited Intercom alternative on the SERP, and for good reason. It's an enterprise-grade helpdesk with a broad integration ecosystem and AI capabilities that have[expanded through acquisitions](https://www.zendesk.com/newsroom/press-releases/zendesk-completes-acquisition-of-forethought/) .


Image source:[Zendesk](https://www.zendesk.com/)


The important thing for ecommerce teams to remember is that Zendesk is a strong helpdesk, but its AI is built for every industry rather than any one vertical. If you switch to Zendesk and still need ecommerce-specific AI resolution, you can add Yuma as an overlay. By doing this, you get Zendesk as the workspace and Yuma as the AI layer, without choosing between switching helpdesks and upgrading your automation.


Pros


- Enterprise scale
- Broad integration ecosystem
- Strong admin and reporting


Cons


- Pricing stacks fast with AI add-ons
- Ecommerce workflows aren't native


**Pricing:** If you want an AI agent, pricing starts from $55/agent/month plus AI add-ons.


### Help Scout


Help Scout is free for up to five users, email-first, and deliberately simple. Its AI Answers add-on runs at $0.75 per resolution with a cap you set, which makes it the closest thing to Intercom's per-resolution model but cheaper and with a ceiling on spend.


Image source:[Help Scout](https://www.helpscout.com/agent/)


A good fit for mid-market teams that handle most support over email and want clean, predictable tooling without the complexity of an enterprise helpdesk.


Pros


- Free tier for small teams
- Clean email-first UX
- Capped per-resolution AI pricing


Cons


- Limited AI depth for autonomous resolution
- Weaker multichannel support


**Pricing:** Free for 5 users, then from $25/user/month. AI Answers costs $0.75 per resolution.


## Budget and small-team alternatives


For teams where Intercom's pricing was always the friction, these options offer core functionality at a fraction of the cost.


### Freshdesk


Freshdesk is the budget helpdesk with Freddy AI for routing and suggestions. It offers a 14-day free trial (no permanent free tier), and the Growth plan starts at $19/agent/month. The interface is relatively simple, which matters for small teams without a dedicated ops person.


Image source:[Freshworks](https://www.freshworks.com/freshdesk/)


Pros


- Low entry price
- [Simple admin](https://www.g2.com/products/freshdesk/reviews/freshdesk-review-13802951)
- Freddy AI for basic routing


Cons


- AI capabilities are shallow compared to purpose-built tools
- Limited ecommerce integrations


**Pricing:** 14-day free trial, then from $19/agent/month.


### Tidio


Tidio combines live chat, rule-based chatbots, and Lyro AI, its[generative AI](https://yuma.ai/blogs/generative-ai-vs-chatbots-understanding-the-difference) layer that goes beyond scripted responses. The free plan includes 50 conversations per month, plus 50 one-time Lyro AI conversations as a trial allowance.


Tidio serves small businesses just starting with automation. That's a different market from mid-market ecommerce brands managing serious ticket volume. Tidio's strength is accessibility and price (the Starter plan runs about $24/month).


Image source:[Tidio](https://www.tidio.com/ai-agent/)


However, pricing can get complex as volume grows, with separate add-ons for Lyro AI conversations, Flows, and branding removal. It also lacks the depth of ecommerce integrations and quality control architecture that scaling brands need.


Good entry point for teams testing AI. Brands that outgrow it are natural candidates for purpose-built tools.


Pros


- Simple setup
- Long history as a strong live chat platform
- Lyro AI offers AI customer service
- Option to build a fully custom AI agent with the help of Tidio's team


Cons


- Pricing complexity at scale, with AI adding expensive add-ons
- Designed for small businesses, so it may not be a good fit for mid-market businesses.


**Pricing:** Paid plans start at $24.17 per month for 100 billable conversations, with pricing for the AI add-on starting at $32.50 per month for just 50 AI conversations.


*See the[Yuma AI and Tidio comparison](https://yuma.ai/compare-yuma/yuma-ai-vs-tidio) for a head-to-head breakdown.*


## How to decide whether to stay on Fin or switch


The decision of whether to keep Fin or switch to another platform may depend on what the Salesforce acquisition changes for your team specifically, and on whether or not there's a better solution out there for you.


**Stay on Fin if** your team is SaaS or product-led, Fin's resolution rate justifies the cost at your volume, and a Salesforce future is neutral or positive for your stack. The acquisition may also give you leverage to renegotiate your contract, since retaining Fin's existing customer base is likely a priority for Salesforce post-close.


**Switch if** you're an ecommerce team that needs depth beyond Shopify, like subscription management through Recharge, returns through Loop, or shipping through carriers that Fin doesn't connect to natively. Or if pricing unpredictability ($0.99 per outcome with no cap) has been a recurring issue, and if an independent roadmap is critical to your[customer service automation](https://yuma.ai/blogs/customer-service-automation) strategy.


**And if you're an ecommerce company?** If your support volume spans Shopify orders, Recharge subscriptions, and return processing across multiple platforms, a purpose-built ecommerce tool covers more of that stack natively than Fin does today. The acquisition doesn't change that. It just makes the timing clearer for teams already on the fence.


Don't forget that if you're already on Zendesk, you don't have to choose between switching helpdesks and upgrading your AI. Yuma installs as an overlay, so you keep Zendesk as the workspace and add ecommerce-specific resolution on top.


## Making the switch from Intercom


Once you've narrowed your list, the evaluation itself matters as much as the choice. Most teams regret a switch not because they picked the wrong tool, but because they tested it on the wrong tickets or didn't test it at all before signing.


Start with your highest-volume ticket type. For ecommerce teams, that's usually WISMO. Run your real ticket data through the alternative and evaluate whether it can resolve those tickets autonomously, meaning it actually takes the action and closes the ticket, not just drafts a response for an agent to review. That's the difference between a tool that saves time and one that saves headcount.


For ecommerce teams on Shopify with Gorgias or Zendesk, Yuma resolves the ticket types that Intercom was never built for, and it installs inside your current helpdesk, so the switch doesn't mean rebuilding your entire support stack. Teams already on Zendesk get the strongest version of this: keep the helpdesk, replace only the AI layer with something built for ecommerce.
